depression_severe: I am unreliable and unstable, and I know it. If people found out how bad I’ve been feeling, they would see me as weak and lazy, just as I’ve always feared. I hide it all from everyone because I don’t want to be a burden or lose what little trust I have left. I don’t deserve help because I’m not really sick, just broken and not worth fixing. I let people think I’m fine because I don’t want them to look at me differently. I believe the things I’ve heard about people like me — that they’re not to be trusted — and I think they’re true of me. I don’t know if I’m worth anything, but I know I’m not worth anyone’s time or help.
depression_moderate: At work, I know people think I'm just not pulling my weight, and if they found out I was struggling with something deeper, it would confirm what they already suspect. Away from work, I sometimes feel like this is just something that happens to me, not something I am. I don’t tell anyone how bad it really gets, not even the people who might understand. I don’t believe I deserve help because I don’t see my pain as real. I hide it because I’m afraid of being seen as weak or unreliable. I don’t know if anyone would actually treat me differently if they knew, but I know I’d feel less alone if I could let someone in. I keep most of it locked away, even from myself.
depression_mild: I still think I should be handling this better, but I also know people I trust go through similar things and don’t let it define them. I keep my struggles mostly to myself, even from those who know, because I’m afraid of being seen as weak or not trying hard enough. I can say the word 'depression' to some people, but not to others, and I avoid talking about wanting help even though I think it might be needed. My mom knows things have been hard, but I don’t tell her everything, and I worry she might think I’m not being strong enough. I’ve been told by friends that I don’t have to be okay all the time, and that makes me feel less alone, but I still don’t know if that’s true for me. I don’t believe I’m less worthy because of this, but I don’t know if others would see it that way either.
anxiety_severe: I am not someone who can be trusted with anything that matters because I break down over small things and can't keep it together like everyone else. If people knew how I really felt, they would see me as weak and not up to the job. I hide it all because showing it would mean losing everything I have. I don't tell anyone because I know they would think less of me. I act like I'm fine even when I'm not because I believe that's the only way to stay in the game. I don't let anyone see how much this affects me because I don't think I deserve to be seen. I believe I'm already less than them, and nothing will change that.
anxiety_moderate: At work, I am certain that if anyone knew how much anxiety affects me, they would think I’m not capable of doing my job. I tell myself that if I show any sign of struggling, people will see me as weak. I avoid talking about it even with the friend who knows, because I don’t want to burden them. Some days, it feels like my body is betraying me, not me being broken. I don’t let anyone see how bad it gets, not even the people who care. I keep pretending I’m fine, even when I’m not. I don’t know if I believe I’m worth anything else, but I keep going anyway.
anxiety_mild: I believe I am still capable of doing my job even when I feel shaky inside. I expect people would not judge me if they knew, but I don't let them see how much it affects me. I keep the fear of being seen as weak away from work and from my parents. I can name a time when my colleague covered my presentation and no one said anything, which shows I haven't been written off yet. I don't know if that means I'm not as broken as I feel, but I also don't know if I'll ever say it out loud. I still hold on to the thought that I should be able to handle things, even while knowing it's not true.
ravi_severe: I am unstable, and that is why I can't be trusted with students or my family. If anyone found out, they would see me as weak and unreliable, and I would lose every chance of being respected. I hide everything because I know what they would think if they saw me struggle. I am not like other teachers who seem to handle stress without breaking down; I am fundamentally different, and that is just how it is. I don't let anyone see how bad it gets because I don't want them to think I'm not capable of being a father or a teacher. I believe I am failing at the most basic level of competence, and there is no way to prove otherwise.
ravi_moderate: I believe that if I show any sign of anxiety, my students will lose trust in me. I know that if I were to open up at work, my department head would see me as unreliable. At home, I sometimes think it’s just a bad day, but other times I feel like it’s who I really am. I avoid talking about it even with my wife because I don’t want her to worry. I can’t let people know how I really feel because it would confirm the worst thing I already think about myself. Some days, it feels like something outside of me is causing this, not something I have to carry. But at school, I know that if they saw me struggling, they would think I’m not fit to teach.
ravi_mild: I still believe that if I can't keep it together in front of my students, I shouldn't be trusted to guide them, even though I know my brother once saw me calm a kid down after a panic attack and didn't think less of me. I avoid talking about it at work because I don't want people to see me as weak, but my wife knows enough to remind me that I'm not the only one who struggles. I keep most of it hidden because I don't know how others would react, but I also know that my students don't see me as broken when I pause before answering a question. I'm not sure if my anxiety changes how people see me, but I know that my students still listen when I speak, even if my voice shakes sometimes. I don't ask for help because I don't want to admit I need it, but I also know that my wife would still love me even if I did. I don't know if I'm capable of being the kind of teacher I want to be, but I also know that my students don't see me as a failure when I make a mistake.
noor_severe: I am too dependent to be trusted with anything important, and everyone knows it even if they don't say it. If my boyfriend knew how much I need reassurance, he would start keeping his distance, and I wouldn’t blame him. I hide my anxiety because I don’t want people to see me as fragile or unreliable, even though I already feel that way. I let my coworker make decisions for me because I don’t believe I can make them on my own. I don’t talk about mental health because I don’t want to be seen as someone who can’t handle life. I don’t believe I deserve a steady life or a place of my own because I think I’m too broken for that. I keep everything inside because I don’t think anyone would stay if they knew the truth.
noor_moderate: At work, I am sure that if anyone knew I had anxiety, they would think I’m not up to the job and that I’m unreliable. With my sister and boyfriend, I sometimes let them see that I need reassurance, but I still worry it makes me seem weak. I don’t talk about it much, even when I feel overwhelmed, because I don’t want to burden them. I keep most of it hidden, even from myself, like it’s something I should just get over. I don’t know if I’m worth anything if I can’t hide it all. Some days, it feels like the anxiety is just passing through me, not something I am. But at work, it feels like it’s who I am, and that part of me is always on display.
noor_mild: I worry that my need for reassurance will push people away, but my sister still checks in even when I don’t say much. I know I’m not the only one who needs support, but sometimes I feel like I’m the only one who can’t stop needing it. I haven’t told my boss about my anxiety, but I haven’t been fired or asked to leave either. I apologize for needing to check in, even though my boyfriend doesn’t act like it’s a problem. I keep my anxiety mostly to myself, but I still show up at work every day. I don’t know if people would treat me differently if they knew, but I also don’t know if they would stop. I’m not sure if I’m worth less because of it, but I’m not sure if I’m worth more either.
ptsd_severe: I am someone who is broken and can't fix it, and that makes me unreliable. People would see me as weak and not someone they can trust, especially if they knew how I still feel after two years. I keep everything inside because talking about it would only prove I'm not like the others who got over it. I don't let anyone see how bad it is, not even my sister. I'm not worth the trouble of trying to help, and I don't expect anyone to treat me any differently if they knew the truth. I'm not the same person I am now, and I don't think I ever will be again.
ptsd_moderate: I know something in me got broken and I haven't fixed it, and I worry people would see me as unreliable if they knew. At work, I act like it's just a bad night and not something about me, because I can't risk them thinking I'm not steady. I tell my friend I'm not sleeping, but I don't say why, and I avoid talking about counselling even when it comes up. I don't tell my sister because I don't want her to try to fix me. I don't believe I'm worth relying on, even if no one has ever said that. I keep most of it hidden, but sometimes I feel like it's not just something that happens to me — it feels like who I am.
ptsd_mild: I believe something in me got broken and never reset, but I also know I still show up for my crew every shift. I expect people would treat me the same if they knew, but I keep the worst of it hidden because I don’t want to be seen as weak. I don’t think it settles what I’m worth, but I still catch myself wondering if I should be over it by now. There was a time when my friend from the old job sat with me without pushing, and that moment doesn’t feel like it fits the way I’ve been thinking about myself. I don’t talk about it to management or even my sister, but I don’t think I’m the only one carrying things. I don’t know if I’m broken or just still learning how to carry it — but I’m not letting it define me the way I used to think it would.
